items.title: Feeding the Matrix Cores: Assembly FP4 GEMM Kernel Design on AMD Instinct™ MI455X GPUs
items.summary: The AMD Instinct™ MI455X GPU raises peak 4-bit matrix throughput four times over the MI355X, while HBM bandwidth rises about three times (specifications, MI355X). A GEMM kernel that was balanced on the previous generation is therefore supply-limited on this one: each byte loaded has to feed more math than before. items.title: Keep the Agent Warm: How ATOM Serves AgentX Workloads on AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs
items.summary: A coding agent makes many model calls in one session, and each one re-sends almost everything before it: one recorded session makes 198 calls, and call #48 sends 195.5K tokens, only 1.3K of them new. Agentic workloads combine long shared histories and short outputs, interrupted by tool calls and parallel sub-agents. Serving them well takes more than raw GPU compute: it means keeping the agent warm, with its history cached and its decode moving when new requests arrive.
